notes: Not adopted. Of the 55 proofs not won that turn, 45 are wins on the true deal too (the deal is not the cause; the CPU's decision used a different deal seed / fell back to search). Only 10 are false proofs (true deal no), from 4 situations; only 2 involve a life trigger (3012157 removed by all variants, 3012218 only by add, to unknown). Each variant removes 1-2 false proofs and loses 36-56 proofs that win on the true deal (mostly win->unknown at 20,000 nodes: defending triggers add opponent branches). Invariant 'proof set must not grow' is violated by both (12) and mode0 (2) because the defensive deal itself changes; add (+1) is sound w.r.t. the old 8 deals (a superset of deals; the gain is node budget freed by failing early on the first deal). Forecast (20-60 fewer proofs, >half not won) matched the count but not the content (2-3% were real false proofs). The remaining 8 false proofs (life 0, defended by hand counters in 3012080 x7 and 3012137 x1) are not explained by the hand slots (the defence-value deal should hold at least those counters); unverified hypothesis: the line depends on my own deck order through my own [On Attack] choices, which the fair deals reshuffle. Next step candidate: a read-only judge that uses the true deal except for my own deck reshuffled. Kept: measurement option true_deal in Game.lethal_json and judge --true-deal. Production arena not needed (moves unchanged; golden/make test confirm).
